articleTitle: LCC-S Compensated Multiphase Wireless Power Transfer System with LC Resonant Circuits for Current Balancing
abstract: To improve the current rating of a high-frequency inverter, multiple phases can be paralleled. Passive paralleling is normally adopted due to its simplicity and effectiveness to balance the phase currents. In this paper, a novel passive current balancing method is proposed to introduce an external LC resonant network between both adjacent phases. In this way, only a small inductance is needed to obtain a very large equivalent impedance to suppress unbalanced currents, and the space inductor structure is easy to expand to multi-phase. The inductor-capacitor-capacitor series (LCC-S) compensated wireless power transfer (WPT) system for electric vehicles is adopted as the application scenario. An experimental prototype is built to verify the effectiveness of the proposed current sharing method.

articleTitle: Cascaded Harmonic Current Control Loop for VSG Harmonic Current Suppression
abstract: When a Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) is connected to a distorted grid, its output current quality is hard to be guaranteed. The existing harmonic control schemes based on PCC voltage sampling, are limited by the small line impedance. To this end, this paper proposes a cascaded harmonic current control loop for VSG harmonic current suppression to allow coordinated closed-loop control of the VSG fundamental voltage and output harmonic current. At fundamental frequency, the VSG follows the fundamental voltage reference of the power loop and controls the output power; at harmonic frequencies, a closed-loop harmonic current compensator regulates the output current harmonics. The output harmonic current closed-loop control is achieved by extracting the harmonic components through a complex vector filter to provide the harmonic voltage reference. It improves the equivalent harmonic output impedance of the VSG and reduces the influence of the distorted grid on the output current. Compared with the existing schemes, the proposed control scheme overcomes the problem of poor suppression due to small line impedance. Finally, a 15kW simulation model is built to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Controller Design and Performance Improvement for Neutral-Point Voltage Regulation Converter of Hybrid Grounding System
abstract: To improve the security and reliability of distribution networks when addressing single-phase ground faults, this paper presents an improved voltage control strategy for hybrid grounding system, taking into account harmonic disturbances. Firstly, the study begins by introducing the active voltage arc-extinguishing principle, the topology and coordinated control of hybrid grounding system. And then, an improved control strategy for the neutral-point voltage regulation converter is further proposed. The methodology incorporates inner-loop PI control for current and outer-loop multi-PR control for voltage regulation. Parallel resonance controllers are introduced to suppress harmonics, with the addition of a lead correction stage to enhance the steady-state and dynamic performance of the control system, effectively achieving fault point arc extinguishing. Finally, simulation results verify the rationality and effectiveness of the improved control strategy and its practical application.

articleTitle: Improved Model Predictive Current Control for PMSM Drives Based on Dynamic Reference Current
abstract: Model Predictive Current Control (MPCC) strategy is a high-performance control strategy for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM), due to its fast response and simple computation. However, traditional MPCC methods often suffer from higher torque and current ripples. In this paper, an improved MPCC control scheme is proposed. Firstly, the control period is divided into n equal parts. Based on the reference current, the optimal voltage vector for the first part of the control period is determined. By utilizing the predicted current with the optimal voltage vector and the motor's electromagnetic torque equation, the estimated speed is obtained. Next, a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller matched with the speed loop is employed to determine the predicted reference current value for the next part of the sub-control period. Using the predicted reference current value, the optimal voltage vector for the next control period is re-selected. This process is repeated n times until the the control period concludes. Finally, through simulation verification, the proposed MPCC method is experimentally compared with the conventional MPCC approach. The results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed MPCC strategy and its effectiveness in reducing current and torque ripples.

articleTitle: Flux-Weakening Control of Synchronous Reluctance Motors
abstract: In this paper, we will firstly introduce the generic flux-weakening control scheme and overview several commonly used flux-weakening strategies for the synchronous reluctance machine. Pros and cons for each method will be addressed. To assure torque control quality during flux weakening operation, a complex vector based current regulation technique is proposed and its command tracking and disturbance rejection performance are evaluated. Finally, overmodulation methods are summarized to maximize the bus voltage utilization for flux weakening.

articleTitle: Dynamic Optimization Method of Distributed Harmonic Compensation Based on Active Device Margin Calculation Model of APF
abstract: With rapid development of power electronics industry, a number of nonlinear devices are connected to the power grid, and the grid voltage suffers from severe harmonic pollution. For the treatment of harmonic voltage, the equipment adopted is Active Power Filter(APF), which can detect the harmonics at the installation point. However, the harmonic sources at each node will vary with time, requiring the injection of new harmonic compensation commands, while also considering the surplus of APF active devices to ensure efficient and stable operation of APF. This paper aims to propose a dynamic adjustment method of distributed harmonic compensation based on the calculation model of active device margin of APF. Firstly, the APF active device loss and injection temperature model is established under different harmonic combinations to calculate in real time whether the harmonic injection command meets the active device margin. Moreover, for the power grid with the harmonic source changes, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to obtain new harmonic injection commands, which on one hand reduces the total voltage harmonic distortion rate of the power grid, and on the other hand meets the active device margin to ensure stable operation of APF.

articleTitle: Research on Transformer Temperature Rise Based on Electromagnetic Thermal Flow Multi physical Field Coupling Analysis
abstract: Usually, the conductivity of transformer windings increases with increasing temperature, so ignoring the variation of winding conductivity with temperature can lead to underestimated winding temperature rise. In response to this phenomenon, this article establishes a three-dimensional electromagnetic thermal flow coupling numerical model for oil immersed transformers, taking into account the influence of winding conductivity changes with temperature, and thus calculating the temperature distribution of the windings. The simulation calculation results show that without considering the process of transformer winding conductivity changing with temperature, the calculation error of winding temperature rise reaches 18.02%, thus verifying the necessity and rationality of the analysis method of the electromagnetic thermal flow coupling numerical model of oil immersed transformers considering the process of winding conductivity changing with temperature, which can provide reference for the temperature rise calculation of oil immersed transformers.

articleTitle: Sorting Strategy for Retired Batteries Based on Voltage Segments
abstract: With the application of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) becoming more and more widespread, how to efficiently and accurately classify and grade retired batteries is the biggest challenge facing the stepwise utilization of LIBs. To shorten the feature extraction time and maximize the battery information, this paper extracts the voltage segment with the largest amount of effective information, which is in the high-rate constant current charge/discharge curve, by using the mutual information index, and extracts 12 characteristic parameters (CPs) on this voltage segment. In addition, since there may be some correlation between different HIs, this paper further eliminates the redundant data by dimensionality reduction through principal component analysis (PCA). Finally, the advantages of the processed data are verified by the fuzzy mean (FCM) algorithm. Experimentally, it is proved that this method can improve the accuracy and speed of clustering well.

articleTitle: Gas Insulated Switchgear Partial Discharge Analysis Based on Optical Detection and Positioning
abstract: Gas insulated switchgear (GIS) has a complex structure and diverse operating environment. Traditional fault diagnosis methods rely on prior knowledge from experts, are susceptible to noise interference, difficult to accurately identify, and are time-consuming and labor-intensive. The optical measurement method is not vulnerable to the interference of electromagnetic waves. Aiming at the problem that the location algorithm is sensitive to the time delay difference and easy to fall into local optimization or misunderstanding, a GIS partial discharge optical detection method based on the improved gray wolf algorithm is proposed. The location model and objective function of partial discharge are given, and the convergence factor of gray wolf algorithm is non-linear, and the hunting behavior is improved. During the simulation process, the feasibility of the improved algorithm was verified under theoretical time delay. By changing the size of the time delay to simulate the actual measurement time delay error, and comparing it with other positioning algorithms, it was found that the average positioning error of the improved Grey Wolf positioning algorithm was 9.21cm, meeting the positioning accuracy requirements. The effectiveness and applicability of the algorithm were further verified through experiments.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Aging in Oil-Paper Insulated Equipment Enhanced by Residual Convolutional Neural Networks Super-Resolved Spectroscopy
abstract: Ensuring stable operation of the power system, the condition monitoring and diagnosis of electrical equipment are paramount. While numerous spectroscopic methods have been adopted for online monitoring and on-site diagnosis, industrial devices, constrained by factors such as size, often lag behind laboratory equipment in key metrics like signal-to-noise ratio and resolution. This can compromise the accuracy of diagnostic results. Addressing this issue, our study introduces a data-driven spectroscopic super-resolution algorithm. By generating extensive training data based on infrared and Raman spectroscopic features, we trained a convolutional neural network, achieving super-resolution reconstruction of low-resolution spectra. This method not only boasts superior performance and high portability but also significantly enhances the performance of compact spectroscopic devices and the accuracy of electrical equipment diagnosis.

articleTitle: Solving Time-Harmonic Three-Dimensional Magnetic Field Problems with Edge Element Method
abstract: Edge elements are finite elements whose degrees of freedom are associated with edges rather than nodes. Edeg elements method allows the tangential component of the vector to be continuous but the normal component of the vector to be discontinuous from one element to the next. In this paper, the edge elements method is introduced comprehensively. Based on the vector basis function, the Galerkin principle is adopted to deduce the A*-A discrete equations of time-harmonic 3-D eddy current problems. Taking a transformer as an example, a three-dimensional model is established to calculate the magnetic field of the transformer by this method.

articleTitle: Neural-Network-Based Predictive Control for PMSM Drives
abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) has gained increasing popularity in the control of motor drives and power converters. However, its control performance deteriorates when there is a mismatch in system parameters. This article introduces a novel neural-network-based predictive control (NNPC) architecture to address this issue. By means of a supervised learning mechanism based on the input-output data of the governed system, the established neural network can replace the original predictive model. In contrast to the standard MPC controller that uses constant parameters to predict future behaviors, the advantage of the proposed method lies in the fact that it can learn the non-linearity of the system and adapt to the parameter perturbations. Consequently, NNPC enhances robustness against parameter variations while maintaining the superior performance of the conventional MPC method. Finally, the proposed method is validated through comparative simulations on a surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor.

articleTitle: Research on Power Quality Optimization of the Microgrid Based on Active Power Filter
abstract: with the large-scale distributed generators (DGs) penetrating in the microgrid (MG), the employment of a number of nonlinear power electronic devices has introduced serious harmonic problems. Therefore, effective power quality optimization methods are of great significance to promote the application and development of clean energy in MG. In this paper, a design scheme of dynamic harmonic compensation based on active power filter (APF) is proposed. Based on the analysis of its structure and working principle, the design methods of key parts, such as harmonic current detection based on d-q transformation, compensation current tracking based on current hysteresis, and DC side voltage control based on PI feedback are developed, and the simulation research is carried out on the MATLAB platform. The waveform results and harmonic analysis data show that APF can effectively improve the current waveform distortion and reduce the harmonic content, so as to realize the power quality optimization of the MG, and thus provide a certain reference value for the following research on harmonic control of the MG.

articleTitle: Research on Insulator Lightning Flashover Arc- Establishing Model
abstract: Lightning strikes can cause flashover and arcing in power line insulators, causing line tripping, equipment damage, power outages and safety risks. This paper uses multi-physics modeling to study the flashover process of line insulators under the combined action of lightning strike impulse and power frequency voltage. By analyzing the potential distribution and heat dissipation of insulators at different stages, it is concluded that suppressing arc formation during the arc building stage of lightning strike can be more effective. It can effectively reduce the arc building rate of insulators.

articleTitle: Research on Position Following System of Robot Joint Motor Based on Current Dynamic Decoupling
abstract: The traditional three-loop control system based on vector control for permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) encounters coupling issues between the direct and quadrature axis currents when applied to robot joint motor drives. This coupling problem leads to instability and oscillations in the current loop, resulting in the motor's inability to achieve fast and accurate position tracking. To address this issue, this paper first introduces the mathematical model of the robot joint servo control system. Then, a control strategy with deviation decoupling is incorporated into the current loop controller to reduce the influence of the coupling term between the d-axis and q-axis on the position tracking accuracy and response speed of the motor. Finally, a simulation model of this control strategy is established in MATLAB/Simulink, and a physical platform is built to verify the effect of this strategy on the response speed of the motor position loop. Both simulation and experimental results have demonstrated that for robot joint servo systems, the vector control strategy with deviation decoupling has no significant impact on position tracking accuracy compared to the traditional Id=0 vector control strategy. However, it significantly enhances the response speed, thereby satisfying the requirements of the robot joint motor position tracking system in terms of response speed.

articleTitle: Digital-Twin-Driven PI Parameter Evaluation Method for Grid-Connected Converters
abstract: Digital twin technology describes and models the characteristics, behavior, formation process and real-world performance of physical objects by using digital technologies such as sensors, Internet of Things (IoT), and artificial intelligence (AI). It is one of the key technologies to realize real-time perception and operation optimization of electric power equipment. Proportional-integral (PI) modules are the most commonly used blocks in the control system of power converters. But choosing the parameters with the best control effect requires repeated experiments. Therefore, this paper proposes a data-driven model that can evaluate the control performance of different PI parameters accurately and efficiently. First, the concept of digital twins and a general architecture applicable to the key power electronic equipment are demonstrated. Then, taking the grid-connected converter as an example, a data-driven model based on artificial neural network (ANN) and Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm is built to realize the evaluation of PI controller parameters. Comparisons with simulation models are also provided to show the validity of the digital-twin driven control parameter evaluation method.

articleTitle: Fiber Optic Distributed Vibration Detection of 220 kV Power Transformer Winding
abstract: Winding is a common part of the transformer failure, its structural deformation caused by the vibration characteristics of the change is closely related to the operating state. The vibroacoustic signals inside the transformer are propagated to the surface of the casing through a complex coupling mechanism of refraction and reflection. Traditional vibration sensors outside the shell are difficult to distinguish the source and size of the vibration sound signal. Aiming at this situation, this paper takes φ-OTDR distributed optical fiber vibration sensing technology as an entry point, and arranges the optical fiber directly on the surface of the transformer winding to study its vibration detection performance. Design and implementation of φ-OTDR-based transformer winding vibration detection programme. 220 kV transformer winding vibration signal characteristic detection under normal conditions is achieved.

articleTitle: An Unbalanced Duty Cycle Modulation for Dual-Bridge Resonant Converter
abstract: This paper proposes an unbalanced duty cycle mod-ulation (UDCM) strategy to optimize conduction loss and improve the overall efficiency for dual-bridge resonant converter (DBRC). Steady-state analysis is performed using fundamental harmonics approximation (FHA), and the ZVS conditions are given. Further, the minimum current trajectory (MCT) is presented, which makes the converter operates with minimum resonant current. Moreover, the ZVS range is extended and the circulating current is well suppressed. The theoretical analysis and calculation are validated through simulation and experimental test.

articleTitle: Datasheet-Based Hybrid Simulation Approach for On-Line Power Loss Estimation of UHVDC Thyristor
abstract: The UHVDC system can realize long-distance and large-capacity power transmission, hence its power loss is important for analysis, which directly influences operating costs. Thyristor losses, as the core loss component of the UHVDC converter station, are challenging to measure directly, especially for real-time operating conditions. Therefore, this paper presents a datasheet-based hybrid simulation approach for estimating UHVDC thyristor power loss in real time. At first, the expression for thyristor power consumption is obtained through a curve-fitting process on the datasheet. Then, the hybrid simulation approach is designed based on the PSCAD-MATLAB interface. The PSCAD model gathers operating point data, while MATLAB calculate this data using a loss estimation algorithm. The proposed hybrid simulation approach is validated through a PSCAD-MATLAB co-simulation with less than 2% loss error compared to the standard method, showing its real-time accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Planning and Design Method of Distributed Harmonic Compensation in Power Grid Based on Active Power Filter Passive Device Margin Calculation Model
abstract: With widely-distributed nonlinear loads in modern power grid, point-to-point harmonics compensation using Active Power Filter (APF) is no longer viable, so that APFs are distributed across the network to minimize the overall nodal voltage harmonics. However, the currently used distributed harmonic compensation planning method does not consider the margin of APF passive devices, so that the theoretical design results are not achievable in practice. This paper proposes a twostep planning and design method considering the passive device margin analytical model. In the first step, the number of APFs and the amount of harmonic compensation are determined, where the optimization iteration stops after all the nodal voltage harmonic voltage are lower than the limits. Then, the APFs passive device is designed according to the proposed APF passive component loss and margin analytical model. In the second step, the particle swarm algorithm is used to optimize the APF installation points and the amplitudes of multiple harmonic orders at each APF, in order to achieve the lowest overall nodal harmonic voltages for the whole network. Herein, the APF passive component loss and margin calculation model is used as the constraints in the iterative process, and also an optimization objective.

articleTitle: Design of Capacitive Digital Isolation Chip
abstract: Isolation refers to the physical isolation of a circuit through transformers, capacitors, and optocouplers, which can prevent DC and harmful AC currents from passing between two parts of the system, but allows for signal and power transmission. By adopting a gate capacitor scheme that can be integrated into standard CMOS processes, compared to using transformers or optocouplers as integrators and traditional discrete device isolation circuits, capacitive isolation can greatly reduce the volume occupied and facilitate miniaturization of related applications. This article proposes a capacitive digital isolator scheme, which achieves good characteristics of blocking interference transmission during digital signal transmission through OOK modulation and FSK demodulation. The specific circuit design is carried out using the Huahong BCD350GE process, which mainly includes two modules: transmitter TX and receiver, and is simulated and verified through Cadence Virtuoso. The simulation results show that the isolation chip can operate normally within the power supply range of 3.3-5V, with a temperature range of −40°C-120°C, a maximum data transmission rate of 25Mbps, a delay of 20.82ns, and a pulse width distortion of 10.11ns. Under a l5pF capacitive load and 5V power supply, the maximum power consumption is l8.91mW.

articleTitle: A New Quantitative Evaluation Method for Flexible Load Energy Conservation Potential of Power System Based on Random Forest Algorithm
abstract: The response potential of power system is difficult to quantify accurately. In order to improve the effectiveness of its quantitative evaluation results, a new quantitative evaluation method of flexible load response potential of power system based on random forest algorithm is proposed. The flexible load model of power system considering user demand is constructed, the function expression of fuzzy rules is obtained through the fuzzy subset of user power load, and the objective function of flexible load of power system is set; The response potential factor of flexible load is calculated based on random forest algorithm. According to the mean value of offset uncertainty and the result of node splitting and updating, the response potential factor under different electricity price indexes and power load is obtained; The quantitative evaluation algorithm of power load impact potential is designed, the comprehensive evaluation indexes are calculated and recorded, and a new quantitative evaluation method of response potential is obtained. The quantitative results obtained from the experiment are consistent with the actual indicators, which shows that the quantitative evaluation method has good accuracy and good practical application effect.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Non-Operation of a DC Arrester Monitor at the Converter Station Pole Bus
abstract: The monitor is connected in series to the earth terminal of the metal oxide arrester and is used to record the number of actions of the arrester as well as the leakage current. JB/T 10492–2011 and GB/T 24845–2018 specify the operating current of the monitor at the standard 8/20 µs waveform, while no requirements are made for other impulse current waveforms. In actual system operation, the current waveform flowing through the arrester is not always the standard 8/20 µs lightning current waveform, which may lead to the situation that the arrester monitor does not operate. In this paper, for the fault case that a DC arrester monitor at the converter station pole bus does not operate, the experimental work was carried out to analyse the causes. The results show that the longer the current waveform and the slower the wavehead, the larger the operating current of the arrester monitor. It is further inferred that in this fault case, the wider (approx. 6.5 ms) duration of the current waveform resulted in a larger current amplitude than that at 8/20 µs test waveform to trigger the monitor operation, and this operating current is likely to be greater than 700 A.

articleTitle: KOA-CNN Based Fault Line Selection Method for Hybrid Grounding System in 10kV Distribution Network
abstract: Aiming at the requirements of fast and accurate fault line selection in hybrid grounding systems of 10kV distribution network, a kind of grounding fault line selection method based on the convolutional neural network of the Keplerian optimization algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the wavelet transform is used to map the zero sequence current signal into a two-dimensional time-frequency diagram to prepare a small current grounding data set. And then, the Keplerian optimization algorithm is used on the convolutional neural network to optimize its learning rate, convolutional kernel size, and number to construct the KOA-CNN small current grounding fault line selection network. Finally, in order to verify the algorithm, the simulation is carried out by MATLAB software, and the results show that the proposed fault line selection method can achieve accurate identification of faulted lines with high reliability.

articleTitle: Control Strategy of LCL Grid-Connected Inverter Based on Hybrid Damping in Weak Grid
abstract: Due to the influence of grid impedance, excessive damping occurs in the grid connected inverter system, and the system will be unstable. In this paper, a hybrid damping control strategy under weak grid conditions is studied for increasing response speed of inverter system, and decreasing harmonic distortion. The hybrid damping control strategy uses capacitor current feedback and capacitor series resistance as damping to suppress the system resonance. The simulation results showed that the control strategy can reduce the influence of the grid impedance on the grid-connected system.

articleTitle: A Half-Dual Bridge Resonant DC/DC Converter with CLC-Type Resonant Network
abstract: Conventional dual active bridge (DAB) converters suffer from high conduction losses due to high backflow power. A half-dual bridge resonant DC/DC converter (H-DBRC) is proposed in this paper to reduce the conduction loss and improve overall efficiency. The converter comprises a full bridge and a half bridge connected through a CLC resonant network, which can reduce the component cost and improve power density. In synergy with the extended phase-shift (EPS) modulation, the converter can eliminate backflow power and achieve unity-power-factor (UPF) operation, which greatly reduces the conduction losses and improves the efficiency. Steady-state analysis of the converter is performed using multiple-harmonies-approximation (MHA) method. A design example based on the analysis results is presented and then verified through both software simulation and prototype experiments.

articleTitle: Verification of Jiles Atherton Magnetization Modeling Theory and Method
abstract: The Jiles Atherton hysteresis model (J-A model) is a mainstream magnetization model that describes the hysteresis phenomenon of ferromagnetic materials. It is widely used in the field of magnetic modeling, which can reflect macroscopic magnetization phenomena and calculate micro energy loss changes. This article derives the characterization form of J-A theory based on the magnetization mechanism and energy conservation equation, and conducts simulation calculations on different material samples. The simulation results are compared with the measured magnetic characteristics data of the material, verifying the effectiveness and accuracy of the J-A model, which can more accurately simulate the static hysteresis loop of ferromagnetic materials.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control Strategy for Direct-Drive Wind Turbine and Energy Storage to Actively Support Grid Voltage
abstract: The reactive power and voltage fluctuation of the power system with wind power have complex characteristics, and the sensitivity of wind turbines to the grid voltage as a typical power electronic equipment brings serious risks to the safe and stable operation of the system. Energy storage (ES) has excellent dynamic characteristics, with wind power for dynamic reactive power support can effectively improve the system voltage. By comprehensively considering the operating characteristics of direct-drive permanent magnet synchronous generator (D-PMSG) and ES, and deeply exploring their reactive power support capabilities, an adaptive control strategy for direct-drive wind turbine and ES to actively support the grid voltage is proposed in this paper. Adaptive droop control is applied to the ES during shallow voltage drop so that it can smoothly emit reactive power to maintain the voltage in the steady state region. When the voltage drop is deep, the reactive power margin of the D-PMSG is fully exploited, and the active power output of the D-PMSG is reduced to increase more reactive power when necessary, which is used to cooperate with the ES for emergency dynamic reactive power support to maintain voltage stability. Finally, a direct-drive wind turbine and ES grid integration system is built on the MATLAB/Simulink platform, and the working conditions of different voltage drop degrees are simulated to verify the effect of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Study on Inter-Layer Current Distribution of 35kV Three-Phase Turnkey Superconducting Cable with Multidimensional Structural Parameters
abstract: In order to study the effect of multi-dimensional structural parameters on the inter-layer current distribution of three-phase turnkey superconducting cable, this paper takes 35kV/2kA three-phase turnkey high-temperature superconducting cable as the research object, and uses the equivalent circuit model to solve the inter-layer current distribution. Through the analysis results, it is concluded that the variation of inter-layer current is related to structural parameters such as winding radius, winding angle and winding direction, in order to obtain uniform inter-layer current distribution, it is necessary to use the opposite direction of neighboring layers, and at the same time, try to ensure that the winding angle of each layer is similar to. These conclusions can be used as a reference for the design of better performance of the cable structure.

articleTitle: SOC Estimation of low-temperature Home Energy Storage Battery Based on PSO-BP
abstract: The maturity of lithium batteries has laid an important foundation for new energy and energy storage industries in recent years. Compared with other methods, lithium battery energy storage has the advantages of small volume, long circulation life, and high energy conversion rate. However, lithium batteries will affect the charging and discharge performance of lithium batteries at low temperature conditions, which will have a certain impact on the estimation of state of charge (SOC). Therefore, the estimation of lithium battery SOC at low temperature is meaningful. Home energy storage lithium batteries are different from vehicle power batteries and energy storage power station batteries. Its working environment is relatively stable and the temperature changes are not large, but there will still be low temperature conditions. This article uses a 100Ah lithium iron phosphate cell as a research object, and obtained the battery cell temperature, voltage, current, and internal resistance data of the battery during the low-temperature charging and discharge process. The back propagation (BP) neural network optimized by particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO) is used to estimate the SOC of the battery. Compared with the general BP neural network and the long-short term memory networks (LSTM) neural network, the balance of the equity rectification is 42.55<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>and 95.97%.

articleTitle: Power Cable Vibration Detection and Signal Feature Parameter Extraction Based on Optical Fiber Mach-Zehnder Interference
abstract: Power cables are widely used in power systems. In order to detect vibration signals of power cables, this paper studies a fiber optic vibration sensing system based on Mach-Zehnder interference (MZI). A 110kV built-in optical fiber power cable was produced, and the internal sensing optical fiber was used to measure the vibration of the cable. The MZI vibration sensor is used to detect the three events of hammering brick, hammering cable, and kicking cable, and compares the signal of the internal optical fiber and the external optical fiber. The vibration signal measured by the internal optical fiber is decomposed by complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN), the characteristic parameters are extracted, and the signal is reconstructed. The experimental results show that the optical fiber vibration sensing system based on Mach-Zehnder interference can be used for power cable vibration detection, which is of great significance to the safe operation of power cables.

Author Keywords: Complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise

articleTitle: Calculation of Magnetic Flux Leakage and Loss of 220kV Transformer Based on MAGNET Field-Circuit Coupling
abstract: Magnetic flux leakage and loss of a transformer reduce the energy conversion efficiency of the transformer, also cause abnormal temperature distribution of the transformer. Studying magnetic flux leakage and loss of a transformer through measurement is a challenging task due to the difficulty of measuring magnetic flux leakage and loss. The finite element calculation makes up for the difficulty of measuring magnetic flux leakage and loss, which is very important for analyzing the magnetic flux leakage loss of a transformer. Based on the actual parameters, a refined three-dimensional(3D) modeling of 220kV three-phase three-winding on load tap-changer oil immersed power transformer in operation is established. The field circuit coupling finite element models of tank and turret are carried out by using professional electromagnetic simulation software MAGNET. Through setting impedance boundary conditions to improve the calculation speed, the distribution of magnetic flux leakage and loss of the transformer under high and medium voltage rated operating conditions is obtained by simulation. The results show that using MAGNET field-circuit coupling analysis can be used to quickly and efficiently calculate and analyze transformer magnetic flux leakage and loss.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Applicability of Flywheel Energy Storage Device Based on the Braking Performance of Urban Rail Trains in High Latitude and Perennial Low Temperature Areas
abstract: Due to the dry winter climate and low temperatures in high latitude and perennial low temperature areas of China, which are significantly different from other regions, the actual operating environment of urban rail transit trains in this region is different from other regions, thereby affecting the braking performance of urban rail transit trains in this region. Due to the strong promotion of energy conservation and environmental protection in China, flywheel energy storage devices have not yet been applied in urban rail transit in high latitude and perennial low temperature areas. Therefore, it is necessary to explore the applicability of flywheel energy storage devices in the special operating environment of urban rail trains in high latitude and perennial low temperature areas of China. This article takes Harbin Metro Line 1 as an example, calculates the total running resistance of the train during operation based on actual operating parameter conditions, and obtains the trend of mechanical braking consuming train kinetic energy under different loads. Finally, the flywheel energy storage results were simulated using the urban rail DC traction power supply simulation platform DCTPS. The simulation results showed that in the special operating environment of urban rail trains in high latitude and perennial low temperature areas of China, the braking energy is relatively abundant. The flywheel energy storage device still has certain applicability in high latitude and perennial low temperature areas of China, and can reduce a large amount of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>emissions. Provide data reference and accumulate valuable experience for the analysis of braking energy and flywheel energy storage devices of urban rail trains in high latitude and perennial low temperature areas of China.

articleTitle: Multi-Machine Equivalent Modeling Method of Wind Farm Considering Multi-Clustering Indexes Such as Ambient Temperature
abstract: Considering the limitations of the wind farm's single-machine equivalent model to accurately represent the operational characteristics of a wind farm, as well as the issue of neglecting environmental factors when selecting clustering indices during the establishment of a multi-machine equivalent model. A multi-machine equivalent modeling method of wind farm is proposed, which takes wind speed, output power and unit ambient temperature as clustering indexes, and combines Canopy algorithm and K-Means++ clustering algorithm. Taking the measured data of a wind farm as a sample, an example analysis is carried out to verify the accuracy of the multi-machine equivalent model and the feasibility of the proposed modeling method.

articleTitle: MMC Equivalent SISO Sequence Impedance Model for Stability Analysis of Interconnection System
abstract: When the modular multilevel converter (MMC) station is interconnected with weak power grids, wind farms etc., broadband oscillation is serious and stability problems are prominent. The AC-side Mingle-Input Mingle-Output (MIMO) impedance models are the basis of the impedance analysis method. They are highly accurate, but the Generalized Nyquist Criterion (GNC) needs to be used during analysis, which is very cumbersome. In this regard, this paper derives the Single-Input Single-Output (SISO) sequence impedance model of MMC to stability analysis, and it is more simpler to apply. Firstly, the d-q impedance model of MMC is developed, and based on it, the SISO sequence impedance model is further derived. The correctness of the above model is verified by frequency sweeping. Finally, the models are applied to the stability analysis of MMC station and weak grid interconnection system. Both theoretical analysis and simulation results show that the SISO sequence impedance model has the same analytical accuracy as the MIMO model, and the analysis process is simpler.

articleTitle: Experiment and Analysis of Electrical Contact Characteristics of Sliding Contacts in GIS Under Multi-Factor Coupling
abstract: The safety and reliability of the electrical connection structure is crucial for the operational stability of GIS equipment. This paper independently developed a multi-factor deterioration analysis test system for electric, thermal and force factors on the contact finger. The relationship between the contact resistance(ECR) of the ML-CUX strap contact finger and the contact pressure, current load, and electrode material was investigated. The temperature variation characteristics of ECR were analyzed under two conditions: fixed deformation and fixed pressure. The findings of this research can serve as a valuable reference for enhancing the reliability of GIS electrical connection structures.

articleTitle: Driving Circuit of Multi-DOF Traveling-Wave Ultrasonic Motor Considering Stray Parameters
abstract: Multi-degree-of-freedom (Multi-DOF) ultrasonic motors can be applied to various precision occasions, and their application is inseparable from a suitable drive device. The special working mode of the ultrasonic motor determines that it has capacitive load characteristics and high-frequency operation. The stray parameters in the circuit cannot be ignored. In this paper, the driving circuit of the multi-DOF traveling-wave ultrasonic motor is designed considering the stray parameters. The circuit includes a push-pull inverter circuit, an absorption circuit, and an LCLC matching circuit. The working principle and the working state of the circuit are explained individually. The feasibility is verified by simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Seismic Resilience of Substation Considering Multiple Uncertainties
abstract: The seismic resilience of substations significantly influences the secure and stable operation of the power system. For example, the Sichuan electrical power grid was severely damaged by the Wenchuan earthquake on May 12, 2008, with direct economic losses of tens of billions of yuan. By analyzing the seismic resilience of substations, the ability of substations to maintain their transform capacity under different levels of earthquakes can be evaluated, and their weak point in substations can be identified. Firstly, this paper presents the case study of a typical 220kV substation in China, using a lightning arrester as a research subject to illustrate the process of determining its seismic vulnerability via seismic shaking table tests. Due to numerous uncertain factors affecting the seismic performance of equipment within actual substations, a newly developed approach that combines the pre-existing equipment vulnerability curves to reconstruct the substation equipment vulnerability curve is presented. Subsequently, the reconstructed equipment vulnerability curves were leveraged to compute the transmission capacity of the entire station. This research bears significance in the construction of a robust power grid.

articleTitle: Reheat Steam Temperature Control of Power Plants Based on Integral Gain Scheduling Under Renewable Energy Integration
abstract: This paper focuses on the control of reheat steam temperature (RST) systems for ultra-supercritical power plants via integral gain scheduling with more and more renewable energy integrated into the power grid. By analyzing the open-loop responses under different conditions and the nonlinearity of the RST system, the necessity of integral gain scheduling is explained. By calculating the stable regions of PI controller parameters, the rationality and reliability of integral gain scheduling are illustrated. Next, simulations under different conditions without/with random load disturbance are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed PID controller. Finally, the robustness analysis further verifies the ability of the proposed PID controller to cope with large-scale variable operating conditions.

articleTitle: Electricity Pilferage Detection Using LoRA RF Module
abstract: Electricity pilferage is a form of non-technical loss due to the criminal act of stealing electrical power, which adversely influences the operation of the power sector. In order to alleviate the aforementioned problem, this study designed a detection system specifically for the presence of illegal wire tampering in the low-voltage distribution power network. The determination of current magnitude is simulated and attained through an IoT (Internet of Things)-based multi-sensor system, and the identification of the presence of electricity pilferage is achieved through the utilization of current sensors and the Long Range Radio Frequency Module, or LoRA. The real-time monitoring, on the other hand, was shown through the programmed webpage through the Master Terminal Unit (MTU). The system shows that the current sensors installed were reliable and efficient in terms of detecting abnormal currents, and LoRA was proven to be effective in terms of its data transmission.

articleTitle: Emergency Control Strategy of Power System Considering Operation Scenario Variations
abstract: Power system emergency control is the core of the second and third defense lines. The deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based control scheme breaks through the limitations of traditional control strategy simulation calculation methods based physical models, and shows great advantages in dealing with high-dimensional nonlinear system control problems. However, there is a lack of research on dealing with the renewable energy grid-connected power system control problem with operation scenarios variations, especially the frequent topological changes. Based on the DRL method, the under-voltage load shedding (UVLS) emergency control scheme considering the operation scenarios variations is proposed. And the graph convolutional network (GCN) is adopted to learn the representation of power grid topological states and solve the problem of topology feature extraction. Moreover, renewable energy grid-connected scenarios with medium proportion, high proportion and extremely high proportion permeability are set up. Case studies on the modified IEEE 39-bus system are employed to demonstrate the performance and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Standardized Check Technology of Information Model for Independent and Controllable Substation
abstract: A comprehensive analysis and combing of the contents of standard check has been carried out for the secondary system information model of a independent and controllable substation, which meets not only the conformance testing requirements of the IEC61850 model, but also the conformance testing requirements of standard engineering application modeling specifications of State Grid Corporation of China (SGCC) and the conformance testing between different application device models. In order to increase the flexibility and speed of model automation checking, two new methods for model static checking are proposed, one is based on the extensible data template and rule, the other on the double nested Hash table. In addition, a check method based on comparison with dynamic memory tree is proposed for model dynamic checking. An automatic model testing tool is developed with the above-mentioned methods. This tool has been successfully used to carry out model checking by testing institutions to improve the comprehensive degree and automation level of the model check.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Localization Method for High-Voltage Cable Based on Affinity Propagation Clustering
abstract: Partial discharge is one of the important characteristics of insulation defects in high-voltage cables, and also exacerbates insulation degradation. Traditional methods for detecting and locating partial discharge in cables have shortcomings such as fast feature attenuation and significant positioning errors. Therefore, a high-voltage cable partial discharge localization method based on affinity propagation clustering is proposed in this paper, which uses the ultra-high frequency electromagnetic wave amplitude generated by partial discharge for localization. Firstly, a simulated partial discharge power source is used to select positioning calibration points at multiple positions of the cable. And the power source discharges, the amplitudes of the discharge signal are recorded in order to establish a calibration database. Then, when partial discharge occurs, it is imported into the calibration database for affinity propagation clustering to calculate the positioning results. Finally, experiment is designed to verify the algorithm proposed in this paper. The experimental results indicate that the average positioning error of the proposed algorithm is about 1 meter, with high localization accuracy and good robustness.

articleTitle: Short-Term Load Forecasting Using Multidimensional Long Time Series: A GMM- LSTNET Approach
abstract: Short-term load forecasting is essential for optimizing energy generation and distribution, aiding in grid stability and reliability, and facilitating efficient energy resource allocation. It also enables timely decision-making in energy management and minimizes operational costs and environmental impacts. This study presents a novel approach for short-term load prediction by integrating the Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and Long and Short-term Time-series network (LSTNET). The proposed method utilizes multi-dimensional feature data from long time series to forecast short-term loads. LSTNET incorporates a traditional autoregressive linear model into a nonlinear neural network component, thereby enhancing the robustness of the nonlinear deep learning model for time series data with irregular scale changes. Additionally, the attention mechanism is employed to tackle the challenge of sequences with unclear or variable periodicity. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in achieving accurate short-term load prediction.

articleTitle: Synthetic Oil Chromatographic Sample Generation for Electric Power Transformer Based on Causal GAN
abstract: Electric power transformer plays a vital role in ensuring the safe, reliable, and cost-effective electric power system. Researching on fault diagnosis related technology for electric power transformers to accurately identify fault types and characteristics holds immense importance for transformer maintenance and the development of appropriate maintenance strategies. However, in real practice, the lack of oil chromatographic data and the imbalanced percentage of fault case data currently impede the development of the electric power transformer health monitoring. In order to solve the problems, we introduce a generation method using GAN (Generative Adversarial Networks) model combining causal mechanism as conditions. We evaluate our proposed method on the quality of synthetic generated data and the accuracy of fault diagnosis comparing with real data. The results show that the proposed method learns from the data and aligned with real-world data but need further improvement.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Detection of Partial Discharge in Power Transformer Based on Fabry-Perot Interference
abstract: In order to monitor the operation status of power transformer in real time and perform ultrasonic detection of partial discharges of insulation faults inside the power transformer, a method of ultrasonic detection of partial discharges in power transformer based on fiber-optic F-P sensing array is proposed. A fiber optic F-P sensor is designed based on the Fabry-Perot (F-P) interference principle. Based on the plate and shell vibration theory, the fundamental frequency of the acoustically sensitive diaphragm of the fiber optic F-P sensing is derived, the vibration model of the diaphragm in single-side contact with the liquid is used, and the resonant frequency of the sensor is measured to be 52 kHz. A mounting method for fiber optic F-P ultrasound sensor using a fiber optic penetrator introduced at the power transformer oil change felling is proposed, and the brackets for the probes are made of wooden boards. Partial discharge experiments were carried out on the real 220 kV power transformer by lifting a metal tip discharge model into the interior of the power transformer and increasing the voltage using the step-up method. The experimental results show that the fiber optic F-P sensing array designed in this paper can meet the requirements of partial discharge detection in power transformer, and the sensor has strong insulating properties and high sensitivity, which can effectively detect partial discharge faults in power transformer.

articleTitle: Research on Short-Term Forecasting of Power Load Based on Improved Genetic Algorithm Optimized BP Neural Network
abstract: With the rapid development of economy, short-term power load forecasting has become an indispensable task for power system in China. In this paper, firstly, considering daily weather factor, a prediction model is established by BP neural network to realize the prediction of power load. Then a genetic algorithm (GA) optimized BP neural network (GA-BP) is developed to achieve the power load prediction. The better prediction results are achieved, compared with BP neural network. Due to the shortcoming of poor local search ability and easy precocity in GA, a improved genetic algorithm optimized BP neural network (IGA-BP) is proposed to optimize power load forecasting model. The example shows that the IGA-BP can effectively improve the accuracy of short-term power load forecasting.

articleTitle: Research on Defect Risk Assessment and Reliability Improvement of Overhead Transmission Line
abstract: In recent years, the design, construction, operation and maintenance technology of overhead transmission line have made great progress, but faults still occur occasionally. According to the analysis of 6650 defect data of overhead transmission lines, the defects of transmission lines have a strong regularity. Based on the defect data, an engineering database consisting of two-level index is established as the basis for risk assessment of overhead transmission line defects. Through sorting out and analyzing various defects in the database, the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) based on expert correction is used to evaluate various defects of transmission lines. The results indicate that the three indicators with the highest risk of transmission line defects are insulators, fittings, towers and ancillary facilities, with a risk impact of 78% on the transmission line. The research results have important reference significance for the key points and schemes of transmission line reliability improvement, so as to improve the safety and reliability of transmission line operation and reduce the probability of failure.

articleTitle: A Heuristic Algorithm Based on Characteristic Analysis for Unit Commitment Problem
abstract: To improve the algorithm performance of mixed integer programming, determining the state of some integer variables in advance is the most direct and effective method. In this paper, we propose a heuristic algorithm based on characteristic analysis of unit and load for unit commitment problem. Starting with the initial state of a given unit, the state of every unit at each time point is examined. Then, the unit is considered to be put into operation when the system positive reserve not be met, and taking the load intersection line across this operation point to obtain all load characteristic values corresponding the unit, such as the load intersection point, intersection point-pair, regression time and so on. Finally, based on the division of load period, the treatment of the unit is determined one by one. By testing the standard examples and practical examples, the proposed method can save about 30% of computing time, which effectively improves the performance of mixed integer programming.

articleTitle: Optimized Method for ESS in Low Voltage Transformer Area with High Proportion PV
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-layer optimization method for configuring energy storage system (ESS) to ensure the stable operation of Low Voltage Transformer Area with high integration of renewable energy sources. Firstly, a hierarchical planning-operation model is established, where the upper layer considers the total cost of ESS planning to determine the rated capacity, and the lower layer minimizes the voltage fluctuation at nodes and network losses to determine the operation strategy of ESS. The Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-III) are employed in a hybrid manner to obtain the optimal planning and operation results of ESS. Finally, simulation analysis is conducted on an actual Low Voltage Transformer Area to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model and method, ensuring the safe and stable operation of Low Voltage Transformer Area with high integration of photovoltaic (PV) energy.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Generator's Third Harmonic Voltage Ratio Grounding Protection Signal Transmission
abstract: Through the analysis of a third-harmonic ratio stator grounding protection signal event during the operation of a 300MW turbo-generator, the principle of the generator's third-harmonic ratio stator grounding protection is explained, and the generator's third-harmonic ratio of the two options is analyzed. Based on the calculation principle of stator grounding protection, suggestions for optimization of fixed value in engineering application and related suggestions for troubleshooting are put forward.

articleTitle: Distribution Characteristics of Electromagnetic Thermal Multi-Field Coupling of Orbital Electromagnetic Launch Devices and Determination of Locations Prone to Ablation
abstract: Orbital electromagnetic launch technology has broad prospects in the fields of military, industry and transportation due to its advantages of fast launch speed, short start-up time and large launch kinetic energy, realizing the maximum utilization of electromagnetic energy. In order to improve the service life and reuse rate of the orbital electromagnetic launch device and solve the positioning problem that is prone to ablation during the launch process, this article first established the equivalent circuit and discharge equation of the orbital electromagnetic launch device and theoretically analyzed its heat primary sources. Based on this, a finite element model of electromagnetic and thermal multi-field coupling is established, and the distributions of the electromagnetic field and temperature field during the launch process are simulated. It is concluded that the current density and magnetic induction intensity are concentrated at the armature groove and tail fin and around the contact points between the armature and the slide rail, and the heat is concentrated at the armature groove and slide rail. These areas are the parts where ablation damage of electromagnetic launch devices is prone to occur. It provides simulation-level guidance for the next step of manufacturing and testing of electromagnetic launch devices.

articleTitle: Digital Twin of Lithium-Ion Batteries for Long Short-Term Memory-Based Temperature Estimation
abstract: Electrochemical energy storage technology represented by lithium-ion batteries is becoming more and more mature, and its safety is attracting more and more attention from academia and industry. The limited resources of the system-on-chip are no longer sufficient for advanced battery management systems (BMS), especially incorporating artificial intelligence algorithms for data governance. To this content, a microservices-based cloud BMS is proposed. Furthermore, we have devised three fundamental microservices: Data Services, responsible for the collection and management of extensive data from the cloud platform; Model Services, dedicated to portraying the behavior of the battery through a digital twin (DT) model; and Algorithm Services, tasked with monitoring the battery's performance metrics. In this paper, we illustrate our approach using core temperature monitoring as an example. We have developed a real-time digital DT for the electro-thermal coupling of lithium-ion batteries, continuously updating model parameters. Additionally, we have crafted a temperature estimation algorithm based on long short-term memory neural networks to facilitate comprehensive battery operation and maintenance throughout its entire lifecycle, ensuring its safety.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Mode Control Strategy of Distributed Static Synchronous Series Compensator
abstract: With the development of new energy grid-connected scale and load diversification, the new power system is faced with the problems of uneven power flow distribution, three-phase unbalance aggravation and line current over-limit. At present, the mainstream solution is to adopt the centralized flexible AC transmission technology which is relatively mature but has poor flexibility and economy. However, due to its own defects, it is difficult to adapt to the dynamic development of the new power system with changeable operation modes and occasions. Therefore, this paper proposes to adopt a distributed static synchronous series compensator with good economy and simple structure to adjust the line power flow, regulate the line current and compensate the line impedance, so as to realize the safe and stable operation of the power grid. In this paper, the topology of DSSC is analyzed, the mathematical model of DSSC is constructed, and the control strategy of DSSC working in multi-mode of power flow regulation, current limit and impedance compensation is proposed. Based on ADPSS, the electromagnetic transient model of 110kV power grid in Guangshui county is constructed, and the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Scheme for Ring-Type DC Microgrid Using Bus-side Capacitor and Positive Line Current
abstract: DC microgrids are becoming increasingly popular due to their compatibility with new renewable energy sources. However, the low inertia of DC microgrids makes them susceptible to faults, which limits their development. The paper proposes a fault diagnosis scheme based on bus-side capacitor current and its Pearson correlation coefficient with positive line current, which can achieve fault detection and fault classification. By utilizing only positive pole information, different fault diagnosis strategies under different fault resistances are proposed. The bus-side capacitor current is adopted to ensure rapid fault diagnosis for low-resistance faults. The Pearson correlation coefficient between the bus-side capacitor current and positive line current is used for high-resistance faults diagnosis. Both the requirements of low-resistance fault diagnosis speed and high-resistance fault accuracy can be satisfied. Meanwhile, the proposed scheme can reduce the number of sensors, which helps to reduce the construction costs of DC microgrids. The feasibility of the proposed scheme has been verified in MATLAB/ Simulink. The faults can be detected and classified within 1.2 ms with high fault resistance up to 10.

articleTitle: Energy Trading Mechanism of Community Microgrid Based on Main-Side Consortium Blockchain
abstract: Considering the distributed characteristics of energy transactions in most microgrid systems, our study proposes a community microgrid energy transaction mechanism based on the main-side consortium blockchain, which aims to encourage honest transactions among diverse transaction entities within the microgrid. To achieve this, we first introduce an aggregation agent to partition the energy transaction scenario into two layers and construct a two-layer energy transaction framework for the microgrid using the main-side chain management approach, which enhances the system's scalability. In addition, we employ electric vehicles (EVs) for energy balancing services, which can reduce the dependence on the main grid in a more economical way and mitigate the negative impact of disorderly charging of electric vehicles on the grid. Furthermore, we design a contribution evaluation mechanism to quantify user contributions within the microgrid system and integrate the contribution evaluation into both the transaction process and the consensus process, which ultimately enhances the quality of distributed trading and ensures the stability of system operations. Through case analysis and numerical simulation, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed transaction mechanism, which shows that it can improve the overall utility of the system. This research has the potential to contribute to the development of sustainable and efficient energy systems.

articleTitle: Cyber-Attack Detection Approach In Photovoltaic Microgrids Using LSTM-based Autoencoders
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) microgrids have been exposed to serious cyber threats for the integration of information and communication technologies (ICT) and renewable energy. In this article, a data-driven detection approach using an LSTM-based autoencoder has been developed against cyberattacks including fake data injection attacks (FDIA) and denial of service (DoS) attacks in PV microgrids. The proposed detection algorithm applies the unsupervised learning method that uses an LSTM neural network to capture the temporal feature and autoencoder to get reconstructed residuals of given input sequence data of measurements. By comparing residuals with the given threshold, the decision can be made on whether the system is attacked. The proposed algorithm has been evaluated for its performance in the PV microgrid model considering PV generation, energy storage system, and grid-tied function under various cyberattacks.

articleTitle: Research on Transformer Multimodal Named Entity Recognition Based on Co-Occurrence Entities and Knowledge Enhancement
abstract: Transformers are important electrical equipment that plays an important role in the three stages of power generation, transmission, and distribution in the power system. Currently, research on transformers is mainly focused on single-modal fields such as images and audio, while research on multimodal named entity recognition is still in its infancy. This paper proposes a transformer multimodal named entity recognition model based on co-occurrence entities and knowledge enhancement to address the issues of image text mismatch and low efficiency of modal fusion in existing methods for multimodal named entity recognition (i.e. Co-occurrence Entities and Knowledge Enhancement, CEKE-MNER). The model adopts cooccurrence entities to solve the problems of image text mismatch and high noise and uses knowledge augmentation to reduce domain knowledge differences to solve the problem of entity semantic divergence. The experimental results on transformer data show that the CEKE-MNER model achieves an F1 value of 82.40% in multimodal data, which is about 2% higher than that in single-modal data; The experimental results on the publicly available datasets Twitter 15, Twitter 17, and Wu Kong CMNER show that the F1 values of the CEKE-MNER model are 72.76%, 85.49%, and 81.96%, respectively, which are higher than the current mainstream multimodal named entity recognition models and have good generalization performance.

articleTitle: A Pilot Protection Scheme for Pole-to-Pole Fault in Flexible DC Distribution Network
abstract: In the flexible DC distribution network, the pole-to-pole fault current has complex and controlled characteristics that challenge fault detection and protection. In the context of the multi-terminal flexible DC distribution network, this paper theoretically studies the short-circuit current characteristics of pole-to-pole fault, derives the analytical expression of the short-circuit current, and analyzes the variation characteristics. On this basis, a fault direction discrimination method based on the polarity characteristics of short-circuit current fault components and a directional pilot protection scheme is proposed. At the same time, countermeasures are put forward for the T-type structure and the special operating condition of the single-ended power supply to improve the protection's applicability and reliability. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can reliably identify faulty lines. The protection principle does not require sampling synchronization and is easy to apply in engineering.

articleTitle: Evaluation Model of Rural Energy Supply Value Chain of Energy Cooperative Based on AHP Analytic Hierarchy
abstract: This paper takes the rural energy supply value chain as the research object, and constructs an evaluation model based on the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) to evaluate the comprehensive benefits of different types of energy cooperatives in the rural energy supply value chain. This paper first analyzes the characteristics and composition of the rural energy supply value chain, then determines the goal layer, criterion layer and scheme layer of the evaluation model, which include five criteria of comprehensive benefit, economic benefit, social benefit, environmental benefit and technological benefit, and four types of energy cooperatives schemes of wind power, solar power, biomass power and small hydropower. This paper uses expert survey method and consistency test method to determine the weights between each layer, then uses AHP to calculate the comprehensive scores of each scheme, and conducts ranking and sensitivity analysis. The results show that wind power cooperatives have the highest comprehensive benefit in the rural energy supply value chain, followed by solar power cooperatives, biomass power cooperatives and small hydropower cooperatives are relatively low. This paper provides a scientific evaluation method and reference basis for the optimal configuration of rural energy supply value chain and the development of energy cooperatives.

Author Keywords: rural energy supply value chain evaluation model

articleTitle: Linear Motor Topology Study and Prospect of Abandoned Mine-Type/Mountain Gravity Energy Storage
abstract: With the escalating demand for renewable energy, the evolution of energy storage technology emerges as a vital trajectory. Specifically, mine-type/mountain gravity energy storage systems, which, due to their large scale, efficient reuse of waste resources, and significant energy storage capacity, present substantial development potential. This study begins by comparing and analyzing both prevailing and newly proposed gravity energy storage technologies. Moreover, the types of linear motor structures adapted to the newly proposed gravity energy storage system are also analyzed. Subsequent comprehensive analysis of current linear motor characteristics seeks to identify the most suitable topology, aligned with motor performance criteria for a specific gravity energy storage system. Finally, a forward-looking perspective on pivotal technologies within mine- type/mountain gravity energy storage systems emerges.

articleTitle: Short Term Photovoltaic Power Combined Forecasting Based on Feature Extraction
abstract: The proposed method aims to address the randomness and volatility of photovoltaic power generation by forecasting short-term photovoltaic power combinations using feature extraction. The method incorporates the firefly sparrow algorithm to optimize the parameters of variational mode decomposition and obtain the signal component with the best forecasting effect. Because the signal components contain different influence characteristics and time series information, the maximum information coefficient is used to screen the characteristics of each signal component, and the feature matrix is established. The zero-crossing rate is used as the index to determine the demarcation point of high and low-frequency signals. The proposed model in the paper aims to enhance the accuracy and stability of short-term photovoltaic power generation forecasting by leveraging the distinct characteristics of high and low-frequency signals. It achieves this by combining the strengths of the long short-term memory neural network and the multi-layer perceptron to handle high and low-frequency signal components, respectively. The model's performance is compared with a baseline model called VMD-LSTM-MLP, as well as other existing forecasting models, under various weather conditions.

articleTitle: State-of-Charge Estimation for Lithium-ion Battery Using Improved Particle Filters
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of energy storage systems, the accurate estimation of battery state of charge stands as a critical component. This paper introduces a comprehensive approach to achieving highly accurate battery state of charge estimation. The foundation of our method is the single particle model with electrolyte dynamics, coupled with a particle filter algorithm, which has proven to be a powerful solution for accurately estimating SOC. To address challenges such as particle degeneracy and the loss of particle diversity, we introduce the particle swarm optimization algorithm, further augmenting the particle filter's performance. The battery is tested under two different types of working conditions, constant current discharge conditions and real-world operational scenarios. The experiment results presented in Section 4 provide compelling evidence of the superior SOC estimation capabilities of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Fast Line Reclosing Strategy for Power System Under DG Access
abstract: For the automatic reclosing of power system under renewable energy source access, the current practice is usually to cut off the renewable energy source or block the reclosing gate after a fault occurs. This will lead to the shutdown of the renewable energy source and the interruption of power supply to a large number of local loads, which is not conducive to the safe operation of the grid and the efficient utilization of the renewable energy source. In this paper, a fast reclosing method is proposed for substation lines with inverter-type renewable energy source access, which can ensure the power supply of important loads and make the renewable energy source stable during the reclosing period without going off-grid. Firstly, it is pointed out that the inverter-type renewable energy source is switched to VSG-control during the reclosing period, so that it has the basic islanding operation capability. Then the method of load shedding with the startup of unloading resistor during the reclosing period is proposed to ensure the power balance between the new energy power and the loads. Next, adjusting the rated frequency of the renewable energy source to accelerate the simultaneous process, which can speed up the whole reclosing process. Finally, the simulations under different working conditions are carried out on the PSCAD/EMTDC to verify the feasibility of the proposed reclosing strategy.

articleTitle: Optimized Valley Skipping Strategy to Improve Efficiency and Reduce THD for DCM Boost PFC Converter
abstract: This article proposes an optimized valley skipping strategy to improve efficiency and reduce total harmonic distortion (THD) for boost power factor correction (PFC) converters in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM). In DCM, the valley skipping strategy is used to reduce the switching ON loss of the power switch. However, conventional skipping strategy causes dynamic changing valleys in a half-line cycle, leading to frequency hopping and extra current distortion. To avoid this, a control strategy based on constant skipping valleys (CSV) is proposed. Firstly, the switching frequency variation with CSV is derived based on the analytical expression of parasitic resonance. Secondly, by employing CSV in control, not only is the switching frequency hopping eliminated, but also the switching cycle corresponds more accurately with the desired cycle. Therefore, an accurate average current control is derived to reduce the current distortion. Thirdly, the CSV is tuned according to a loss estimation, which further improves the efficiency under valley skipping operation. Finally, a 250W prototype is built to verify the proposed control strategy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy improves the efficiency by an average level of 0.4% and reduces the input current THD to levels below 3.1% at rated power.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Planning of Large-Scale Offshore Wind Power Integration System Considering the Cumulative Effects of Typhoons
abstract: Aiming at the planning problem of large-scale offshore wind power integration system considering the cumulative effects of typhoons, a bi-level multi-objective planning model of large-scale offshore wind power integration system is proposed. Firstly, the Gumbel extreme value type I distribution and the cumulative impact time of typhoon are adopted to propose the line failure rate under the cumulative impact of multiple typhoons. On this basis, a bi-level multi-objective planning model of large-scale offshore wind power integration system considering resilience improvement is constructed. The upper model aims to minimize the total cost of investment and operation cost, resilience improvement cost, and load loss penalty under the cumulative impact of typhoons. The typhoon weather is regarded as a participant in the game in the planning, and the zero-sum game planning model of offshore wind power integration system planning system is constructed. In the lower model, combined with the line failure rate under the cumulative influence of multiple typhoons, the system resilience is improved by considering the minimum total load shedding of the system during the typhoon transit. A two-stage relaxation algorithm is used to solve the built model. and the two-stage relaxation algorithm is used to solve the model. Taking an offshore wind farm group integration system planning as an example, the simulation is carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model and method.

articleTitle: Data Augment Method for Power System Transient Stability Assessment Based on DeepSMOTE
abstract: Data-driven transient stability assessment (TSA) method has become the focus of power system stability and security research in recent years. However, in actual power system, transient unstable data only accounts for a small portion of all data.
